item.title: AMD's 256-core monster EPYC CPU is its most expensive processor ever launched — 600W 'Venice' 9996 has 1 GB cache, supports PCIe 6.0 and MRDIMM, both cutting-edge enterprise-only tech that probably won't come to consumers until after 2030
item.description: At $14,904, it clocks in exactly $91 more than the chip it replaces from AMD.

item.title: Musk’s AI chatbot Grok reportedly encouraged Trump to capture Venezuela’s president
item.description: President Trump reportedly asked for Grok's opinion before invading Venezuela and capturing Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: Samsung launches its first clip-on earbuds in South Korea
item.description: A global rollout will follow, although we don't yet know the details.

item.title: The Best Early Prime Day Deals Ahead of Amazon’s Second Sale (2026)
item.description: Amazon Prime Big Deal Days officially begin on October 6 and 7, but I’ve already spotted early discounts on gear our team recommends.

item.title: Metro 2033 and Metro: Last Light remasters are getting free next-gen updates this month
item.description: Take a trip down memory lane with the first two games in the series.

item.title: Police may have new ways to access data on locked iPhones
item.description: A training video reportedly demonstrates how police can evade an Apple security feature.

item.title: Microsoft deletes nonprofit customers' M365 data — and says it can't get it back
item.description: Nonprofit organizations using the Microsoft 365 Business Premium Grant found their data had been deleted early after Microsoft advised they move to a different licensing plan

item.title: Oura partners with Xella Health to combine your smart ring data with AI-powered biomarker testing
item.description: Oura has a new partner integration, and this time it’s a women's health platform that combines lab testing with telehealth care, dubbed Xella Health.

item.title: Does You Can See Everything live up to the hype?
item.description: Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes make a mesmerizing and mind-bending match in "You Can See Everything." Review.

item.title: More than 1 in 3 Americans making over $300,000 say they are living paycheck to paycheck
item.description: A new Goldman Sachs survey finds even some of the country’s highest earners are struggling to save and delaying major financial goals. The affordability crisis puts a huge strain on Americans making the least, but apparently everyone is feeling it.

item.title: Trump’s ‘Morally Binding’ AI ‘Accord,’ the Rise of AI Agents, and Extremists on the Ballot
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we discuss the voluntary AI safety agreement tech executives signed, AI agents for normies, and extremist candidates running for office in the US midterms.

item.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
item.description: Guided Vision is launching in Gemini Live on compatible Android devices today to use AI to give real-time audio descriptions of anything you point your phone's camera at.
